surprises.head: Colorado couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Colorado’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.8% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 100 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: The Devils beat the Avalanche
paras: Connor Brown played his first game of the season, after missing the first eight, and picked up an assist. Luke Evangelista opened the scoring for the Devils midway through the first, but Gabriel Landeskog made it 1-1 for Colorado late in the period. Declan Chisholm scored his first goal for New Jersey midway through the second to put the Devils ahead for good. The third period was a wild one. Arseny Gritsyuk made it 3-1 early in the period. Jesper Boqvist added an empty-net goal with just under four minutes left to make it 4-1, but that didn’t stop Colorado. Artturi Lehkonen scored with a little over three minutes left and again just over three minutes later to cut New Jersey’s lead to 4-3, but the Avalanche couldn’t find another.

The Devils drove the play, outshooting the Avalanche 41-34, and the scoreboard caught up. Jake Allen made 31 saves for the Devils, and Scott Wedgewood stopped 37 of 40. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Nico Hischier, by our Swing measure.
Only two penalties were called all night, something the league sees about once every 20 games. The Devils improved to 5-4-0, and the Avalanche fell to 5-4-1.

items.text: Artturi Lehkonen has a point in five straight games.
